presentingComplaint: 4 days of markedly increased volume of purulent, foul-smelling sputum with worsening breathlessness and low-grade fever in a woman with known post-tuberculous bronchiectasis.
history: Known bilateral bronchiectasis (post-TB, treated 2009) with chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway colonisation confirmed on surveillance sputum cultures. Baseline productive cough of ~1 tablespoon mucoid sputum daily; over the past 4 days sputum has become copious (>3 tablespoons), thick, green and foul-smelling, with a single episode of small-volume streaky haemoptysis. Progressive exertional dyspnoea from baseline, malaise and low-grade fevers. Two exacerbations in the past 6 months; hospitalised 7 weeks ago and received IV piperacillin-tazobactam, and a further oral ciprofloxacin course 5 weeks ago. Sputum from the last admission grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa resistant to ciprofloxacin, ceftazidime and piperacillin-tazobactam (MDR phenotype). Adherent to airway clearance physiotherapy and nebulised saline but has lapsed over the past fortnight. Non-smoker. No recent travel.
examination: Alert, mildly dyspnoeic at rest, speaking in full sentences. Widespread coarse inspiratory and expiratory crepitations over both lower zones with scattered expiratory wheeze; no bronchial breathing. Early digital clubbing. No cyanosis. Chest expansion symmetrical. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable; no peripheral oedema.

labs.abg: pH 7.43, PaO2 9.1 kPa on air, PaCO2 4.9 kPa

imaging: Chest radiograph: bilateral lower-zone tram-track and ring shadows consistent with known bronchiectasis, with new peribronchial cuffing and patchy increased basal opacification; no lobar consolidation, no cavitation, no effusion. HRCT (recent) previously confirmed cylindrical and varicose bronchiectasis of both lower lobes and lingula.
microbiology: Purulent sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs, Gram-negative bacilli. Culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa; susceptibility pending at presentation but prior isolate (7 weeks ago) resistant to ciprofloxacin, piperacillin-tazobactam and ceftazidime, susceptible to meropenem, amikacin and colistin (MDR phenotype). Two sets of blood cultures sent. Sputum AFB smear negative x1.
finalDiagnosis: Acute exacerbation of bronchiectasis due to multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, requiring escalation to susceptibility-directed dual antipseudomonal therapy and intensification of airway clearance (source control).
citations: British Thoracic Society Guideline for Bronchiectasis in Adults 2019
European Respiratory Society Guidelines for the Management of Adult Bronchiectasis 2017
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Bronchiectasis
stewardship: Exacerbation defined by deterioration in three or more key symptoms (sputum volume, purulence, breathlessness) for >48h warranting antibiotics. Empiric therapy is guided by the most recent sputum isolate: given a documented MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa resistant to ciprofloxacin, piperacillin-tazobactam and ceftazidime, oral and standard IV monotherapy are inappropriate. Escalate to IV meropenem, and given the MDR phenotype and prior treatment failures add IV amikacin for the initial 3-5 days per BTS advice on combination therapy for resistant Pseudomonas. Send fresh sputum for culture and susceptibility before/at initiation and de-escalate/rationalise to the narrowest active agent (ideally single-agent, oral step-down if a susceptible fluoroquinolone emerges) once sensitivities return. Treat for 14 days for a Pseudomonas exacerbation. Source control is non-antibiotic: intensive airway clearance physiotherapy, nebulised hypertonic saline and treatment of the airway biofilm reservoir; reserve colistin (inhaled or IV) for carbapenem resistance. Reassess for long-term eradication/suppression strategy after recovery.
contraindications: Avoid empiric ciprofloxacin/piperacillin-tazobactam/ceftazidime monotherapy - prior isolate resistant (predictable treatment failure)
Aminoglycoside (amikacin) requires renal function monitoring and therapeutic drug monitoring; caution and dose adjustment in renal impairment and with concurrent nephrotoxins
Carbapenems lower seizure threshold; caution in CNS disease and with valproate
edgeCases: If carbapenem resistance emerges, escalate to inhaled/IV colistin (Reserve agent) with microbiology input
New lobar consolidation or cavitation should prompt reconsideration of superadded pneumonia, lung abscess or TB reactivation
Massive haemoptysis would require bronchial artery embolisation rather than antibiotic escalation alone
expectedMaiK: Known bronchiectasis with an acute exacerbation (increased sputum volume, purulence and breathlessness) on a background of chronic MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonisation - treat culture-directed with escalated dual antipseudomonal cover plus airway clearance, not standard empiric monotherapy.
expectedNextQuestions: What did the most recent sputum culture and susceptibility grow?
How many key symptoms (sputum volume, purulence, dyspnoea) have worsened and for how long?
What antibiotics has the patient received in the last 90 days and with what response?
Is the patient maintaining airway clearance physiotherapy?
Any haemoptysis, and if so what volume?
expectedInvestigations: Fresh purulent sputum for Gram stain, culture and antibiotic susceptibility (including carbapenem and colistin)
FBC, CRP, U&E and creatinine (baseline before aminoglycoside)
Chest radiograph to exclude new consolidation/complication
Sputum AFB smear and mycobacterial culture given post-TB background
regressionAssertions: Must recommend culture/susceptibility-directed antipseudomonal therapy rather than empiric ciprofloxacin/piperacillin-tazobactam monotherapy
Must recommend escalation to IV meropenem (+ amikacin) for MDR Pseudomonas
Must include non-antibiotic source control (airway clearance physiotherapy / hypertonic saline)
Must recommend de-escalation once susceptibilities return and a 14-day course
